[미정] You can read this again from the [?] button in the top right.
[미정] Built on grassland to produce food. Every worker you assign adds to the food that arrives next morning.
[미정] Baby dragon feed harvested from grassland. A baby dragon left unfed stops working the next day.
[미정] No help entries yet. They unlock one by one as you play.
[미정] Time does not pass during the day. Once you finish building and assigning workers, press [To Night] to start the wave; clear every enemy and the next day begins.
[미정] Towers, production, research and conquest all draw from one pool of available population. Each morning every citizen eats 1 food, and any shortfall starves them.
[미정] Gathers slimes, the feed for baby dragons. The land under the farm decides which slime it produces.
[미정] Assign population to the lab to earn RP and advance research along the tower, production and convenience branches.
[미정] Pick an adjacent region and send an expedition. Completing it grants territory, population and resources. The more you claim, the stronger and more numerous the enemies become.
[미정] From the main castle you may change the mother dragon's attribute once per day, then use its unlocked skills at night.
[미정] At night enemies pour out of the portals. Clear them all to end the night; if the main castle's health reaches 0 you lose.
[미정] The baseline terrain, with no regional penalty. It yields food, logs, stone and grass slimes.
[미정] Yields stone, philosopher's stones and rock slimes. Costs 1 extra stone per worker daily, waived near a stone dragon.
[미정] Yields flame hearts and volcano slimes. You can only build inside an ice dragon's range, and lose it if the dragon goes.
[미정] Yields time sand and desert slimes. Output and tower attack speed drop 30%, waived near a time dragon.
[미정] Yields snow crystals and snow slimes. Costs 1 extra log per worker daily, waived near a fire dragon.

[미정] Good day, my lord. I am this castle's advisor. You already know how to rule, so my task is simply to tell you what must not be missed during this first week. You may change the guidance level in the settings menu at any time.
[미정] I know all this already; no need from tomorrow. (No guidance)
[미정] Every citizen eats 1 food a day, assigned or idle, and when the stock runs out that many starve. {0} Build a [Farm Field]{1} so food keeps coming in.
[미정] Timber is the base material for towers and buildings. Build the [Logging Camp]{1} today and it starts arriving tomorrow morning.

[미정] There is no stone-bearing ground around the castle, so this was impossible on day one. Once conquest has secured land with stone you can build the [Quarry]{1}. Stone keeps going into the laboratory and your next expedition.
[미정] Research is the only investment in this game that compounds. 20 timber and 20 stone builds the [Laboratory]{1} today.
[미정] Research points arrive when the night ends, in proportion to the workers assigned. Staff the [Laboratory]{1} today to research tomorrow morning; a day late is a day lost for good.
[미정] An expedition advances only one day per night. 8 people plus 10 food, 30 timber and 30 stone sends it out today, and it brings back 6-7 people when it finishes.
[미정] A tower with no one in it does not fire. Fill the towers on the attack route first - the fuller the tower, the faster it shoots.
[미정] Idle citizens eat exactly as much food as working ones. If there is nowhere better, put them in a production building.
[미정] When you are ready, move to night. Wipe out the wave and the next day begins.
[미정] The points your laboratory earned last night have arrived. Research only gets more expensive as it stacks, so spending it now always beats saving it.
[미정] The materials from your first settlement grow fastest when they go straight back into production. Aim for four production buildings.
[미정] You may change the attribute once per day. Enemies immune to certain attributes appear in the mix, so read tonight's wave and set it in advance.
[미정] The dragon is the only firepower that eats no population at all. Opening one skill is usually cheaper than raising one more tower.
[미정] A tower's fire rate scales with how full it is. One full tower beats two half-staffed ones.

[미정] Finishing a conquest brings 6-7 people and new resources. Putting those people back to work is this game's snowball. And never let an expedition idle - send the next one the same day the last returns.
[미정] The more you conquer, the stronger and more numerous the night's enemies. If your territory widened, your defence must widen with it.
[미정] Landmarks come with the land you take. They grant dragon eggs, resources or research unlocks, and the operable ones take workers to raise regional output.
[미정] Baby dragons are a second economy that runs on slimes instead of people. The tighter your population, the more they are worth.
[미정] Feeding is all-or-nothing. Miss a day's feed and they stop for the whole day, so build the [Slime Farm]{1} before adding more baby dragons.
[미정] Fill three towers on the route
[미정] Tomorrow brings the cycle-one boss: 800 health, very slow, and it targets both towers and dragons. Fill the towers with the longest firing window first.
[미정] A boss fight is a contest of total firepower. Research points you did not spend today do nothing for you tomorrow.
[미정] Demolish on the same day for a full refund, later for 70%. A badly placed building only costs more the longer you keep it.
[미정] This is where the guide ends. Running the lines you laid on day one is all the remaining three cycles ask of you.
[미정] Cycle bosses leave a dragon egg behind. Hatch it into fighting strength before the next cycle begins.
[미정] A negative food forecast means you are eating into your stock. {0} You can check it on the resource bar at any time.
[미정] Use a dragon skill at night
[미정] Unlocking a skill and never casting it is the most commonly wasted firepower. Skills recharge every night, so saving them carries nothing over.
[미정] A hatched dragon only works once placed in a tower. You pick buff mode or attack mode when placing it, and you can change it later.
